proof: For each particle, images of each other particle form a shifted L-lattice. Disjoint cubes of side L centered at images inside B(r) fit into B(r+a), a=sqrt(3)L/2. Their count n(r) is <= C(r)=(N-1)*4*pi*(r+a)^3/(3*L^3). Integration by parts gives sum_{distance>R}g(distance)=-g(R)n(R)+integral_R^infinity n(r)*(-gprime(r))dr <= integral_R^infinity C(r)*(-gprime(r))dr. Omitting self images is exact for a graph action. The omitted PSD graph norm is bounded by twice its maximum weighted degree, then by twice its maximum degree trace. physical_tail_bound evaluates the resulting analytic integral for g=exp(-.2*r)/r. Radius uses a physical minimum-image graph norm lower bound, so the norm ratio criterion is conservative.
lower_norm_proof: The minimum-image physical graph is a PSD summand of the full unsplit graph. Its maximum eigenvalue is a lower bound on the full graph norm and on each direct partial sum containing all minimum images.
kernel_correspondence: E.kernel(.2,xi,0) creates RadialEwald(law=A,kappa=.2,amp=1); theta_full(r)=exp(-.2*r)/r. direct_unsplit_dense independently evaluates exp(-.2*r)*d*d.T/r^3. theta=0 removes every isotropic shift. Neither path uses common.py LJ amplitude or kappa=.7.
floating_point_scope: Analytic truncation bound in real arithmetic; summation and evaluation floating point errors are not claimed as interval-certified. Unit tests compare independent sums and graph assemblies.
